items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: Earl Bostic was a very gifted young man. He would appear on Saturday night, amateur shows... So the church gave Earl a clarinet... he got a scholarship to Xavier University... he left there and he went New York.

ctx.x: The instrument was about four feet wide -- I mean, not four feet, four inches wide and about four inches in depth. But the bottom was vacant. It doesn't have a back on it. This was for beginners for violin class. So, my mother bought me one and I couldn't stand that squeaking. And I left it in my locker all the time. I missed all my classes. So my mother says, "When are you going to bring your violin home and let me hear you play it?" I say, "Well, I'll bring it home when I think that I can play it to satisfy…

So, how I started playing trumpet. Earl Bostic was a very gifted young man. He would appear on Saturday night, amateur shows, you know, and he'd play the part of Harold Teen. He had the big leg pants and he'd whistle and play ukelele. win first prize And he'd always (unintelligible). So, he was a Catholic, but he was going to public school, because our Catholic school didn't go any further than about sixth grade. But they had instruments.

So the church gave Earl a clarinet so that he could play in the public school band. And Earl picked it up in no time, and he got a scholarship to Xavier University in New Orleans. And when he graduated, he graduated and stayed on as bandmaster for about two years, and he left there and he went New York.
